history.dynasty: Kulasekharam (legendary); Travancore era patronage; refurbished 1921 by Sreemoolam Thirunal
history.period: No written history survives; local tradition claims up to 4,500 years based on wall inscriptions (Vattezhuthu/Kolezhuthu) - UNVERIFIED; mentioned in the Travancore Archaeological Series (1916)
history.summary: Thrikkakara Temple, between Edappally and Pookattupadi, is one of the very few temples in India dedicated to Vamana, the dwarf avatar of Vishnu, and the principal centre of Onam celebrations. Legend holds this is the spot where Vamana took the third step of land on King Mahabali's head and pushed him to Patala; 'Thiru-kaal-karai' (land under the holy feet) became Thrikkakara, and the genesis of Onam is marked here. Local tradition credits Parasurama with installing the deity after bringing Brahmins from the north to settle here. The Kerala Tourism account records that Kulasekhara emperor Cheraman Perumal Bhaskara Ravi Varma held annual assemblies of 56 kings and 64 chieftains at Thrikkakara during a 30-day festival, and decreed that Onam be celebrated everywhere with the Thrikkakara deity - the origin of the household Onam celebrations. The temple declined after the 12th century during royal disputes and was refurbished by Sreemoolam Thirunal in 1921. It is counted among the 108 Divya Desams. Antiquity claims (4,500 years from inscriptions) are unverified by any source consulted. CSV town corrected: the temple is at Thrikkakara, a suburb within the Kochi urban area.

name: Thrikkakara Temple
town_description: Thrikkakara is a suburb in the northeastern part of Kochi, Ernakulam district, on the road between Edappally and Pookattupadi near National Highway 66. It is home to the famous Vamana temple that gave Onam its spiritual centre, and has grown into a modern IT and residential hub (including Infopark Kochi). The Onam festival week here draws devotees from across Kerala.
